episode_title: #90 - Polen-special: börsrallyt, våra kunders favoritbolag och deepdive av Dino Polska!

stock_segments.discussion_summary: Dino Polska is Poland's fastest-growing grocery chain with a market cap of ~100 billion SEK. Founded in 1999 by the reclusive Tomasz Biernacki who owns 51% of the company. The company operates ~3,000 standardized 400 sqm stores located in smaller Polish cities and rural areas, targeting underserved markets. Unique business model includes owning 95% of stores and land, owning meat processing operations, and having an affiliated construction company (personally owned by founder) that builds identical stores. Never closed a store. Financials show strong performance with 27% gross margin, 9% EBITDA margin, 15.2% revenue growth, and ROIC above 20%. Stock is down 25% from peak, now trading at P/E 24 vs historical P/E 35. Concerns include declining like-for-like growth, increasing competition from Lidl, Biedronka, Carrefour, potential margin pressure, and limited online presence. Company reinvests all profits into expansion with no dividends or buybacks.

bull_case: Standardized 400 sqm stores in underserved rural/small city markets
Vertical integration with own meat processing (Agro Rydzyna)
Owns 95% of stores and land - no rental costs or future rent hikes
Construction company (Krotinvest) enables rapid, cost-effective expansion
Never closed a store - proven store format
High margins (27% gross, 9% EBITDA, 6.4% EBIT) vs Swedish peers (~4%)
Strong revenue growth (15.2%) and expected 17% CAGR through 2028
Poland growing at 3-4% GDP, 38M population, 50% of savings on bank accounts
Now at lowest valuation since IPO (P/E 24 vs historical 35)
bear_case: Like-for-like growth declined from double digits to 4.5% in 2025
Real L4L growth near zero after adjusting for 4.6% food inflation
Increasing competition from Carrefour, Lidl, Biedronka
Price pressure from more competitors could compress margins
Limited online presence (just acquired Easy Bra as first step)
Rising wages in Poland will pressure margins inevitably
Stock down 25% from peak due to concerns about growth and competition
Risk of margins converging toward Swedish levels long-term
Market not yet saturated but unclear how many stores Poland can support
catalysts: Continued store expansion (290 stores planned for 2025)
Poland GDP growth of 3% expected through 2030
Online expansion through Easy Bra acquisition
Potential Ukrainian reconstruction benefit when war ends
Polish investment savings account (similar to Swedish ISK) could drive capital inflows to Polish stocks
risks: Competition from Lidl, Biedronka, Carrefour intensifying
Margin pressure from competition and rising wages
Concentration risk with 51% owned by founder
Construction company (Krotinvest) not owned by shareholders

stock_segments.discussion_summary: Bank Pekao is Poland's largest and oldest bank, founded in 1919. Employs ~26,000 people with nearly 1,000 offices. Offers banking and insurance services for consumers and businesses. Consumer loan interest rates around 12% per year. Features automatic savings features (round up, percentage, random joker). Strong ROE of 19% (trailing 12 months). P/E around 10, similar to Swedish banks. Price-to-book at 1.8x, higher than historical 1.3x average. Compared to Handelsbanken which historically targeted 15% ROE. Valuation has come up compared to historical averages.

quotes.text: Vill man låna pengar så är räntan strax under 12% om året.

quotes.speaker: Niklas
quotes.text: Och sen P-talet då, det ligger strax under tio. Så det känner man ju igen egentligen från svenska banksektorn också.

quotes.speaker: Niklas
quotes.text: Här handlas den till 1,8 gånger bok. Och snittet senaste både tre och fem åren har varit runt 1,3 gånger bok. Så det här ska man nog ha med sig att värderingen har kommit upp en delar.

bull_case: High interest rates (~12% on consumer loans)
P/E around 10 similar to Swedish banks
bear_case: Price-to-book at 1.8x, higher than historical 1.3x average
Valuation has come up from historical levels
Bank sector always has regulatory and economic cycle risks
catalysts: Polish ISK/savings account could increase capital in market

stock_segments.discussion_summary: Warsaw Stock Exchange (GPW) is Poland's stock exchange founded in 1817, with modern era starting 1991. Largest exchange in Central and Eastern Europe with ~400 companies. Total market value around 6,000 billion SEK vs Stockholm at 15,000 billion SEK. Revenues expected to grow 8% per year, profits 10%. Operating margin 27% and ROIC 14%. Compared to Stockholm exchange which has ~410 companies.

quotes.speaker: Niklas
quotes.text: Warsaw Stock Exchange som man hittar genom att skriva GPW. Det är Polens börs som grundades 1817. [...] Det här är den största börsen i central- och östeuropa med ungefär 400 bolag. Och ett marknadsvärde totalt sett på runt 6 000 miljarder kronor.

quotes.speaker: Niklas
quotes.text: Här tror man att intäkterna spås öka 8% per år framåt. Vi har ju estimat i 2028, samtidigt som vinsten spås öka 10%. [...] Rörelsemarginal på 27% och en ROJC som du var in på här nyss på 14%.

bull_case: Largest exchange in Central and Eastern Europe
bear_case: Smaller market cap vs Stockholm (6,000B vs 15,000B SEK)
Exchange dependent on overall market performance
catalysts: Polish ISK could drive more retail investment
risks: Exchange dependent on broader market conditions
Smaller scale vs Western European exchanges

stock_segments.discussion_summary: CD Projekt Red is a Polish gaming company known for global successes like The Witcher series (75 million copies sold for entire series) and Cyberpunk 2077 (35 million copies). Owns GOG.com, a DRM-free digital distribution platform (like Epic Games or Steam but without DRM - customers own files outright). Stock up 32% this year. Operating margin 45% and ROIC 18%. Gaming sector seeing some tailwinds from low levels.

quotes.speaker: Niklas
quotes.text: Det här är ett gamingbolag som utvecklar spel och mest kända är man väl kanske för globala succéer som The Witcher-serien. Som har sålt i 75 miljoner X för hela serien då. Och Cyberpunk 2077 som har sålt 35 miljoner X.

quotes.speaker: Niklas
quotes.text: Dessutom äger man gog.com, som är en DRM-fri digital distributionsplattform. Tänk Epic Games eller Steam, men utan DRM-skydd, som då står för Digital Rights Management. Det här innebär att man äger filerna fullt ut. Man kan installera dem och använda dem utan internetuppkoppling och göra säkerhetskopier och flytta mellan enheter.

quotes.speaker: Niklas
quotes.text: Aktien är upp 32% i år, rörelsemarginalen på 45% och en ROJK på 18%

bull_case: Gaming sector seeing tailwinds from low levels
catalysts: GTA 6 launch expected next year could boost sector
risks: Hit-driven industry requires constant new IP

stock_segments.discussion_summary: iFirma offers cloud-based accounting and invoicing services for small businesses and sole traders in Poland. Reminiscent of Fort Knox. Revenues grown 22% CAGR in last 5 years, profits 32% CAGR. Operating margin nearly 26% and ROIC 61%. Stock up 28% this year and 455% in 5 years.

quotes.speaker: Niklas
quotes.text: Driver webbplattformen ifirma.pl och får den att tänka på Fort Knox. Intäkterna har växt med 22% i kaggar i de senaste fem åren och vinsten med nästan 32% kaggar. Rörelsemarginalen på nästan 26% och en ROJK på 61%. Aktien 28% i år och 455% på fem år.

bull_case: Strong growth: 22% revenue CAGR, 32% profit CAGR

summary: This episode focuses on Poland as an investment destination, with a deep dive into Dino Polska. Poland has shown strong GDP growth of 4% since 1990 and is expected to grow 3% through 2030. The Polish stock market is up 40% YTD. The podcast discusses the top 10 Polish stocks owned by their customers, with Bank Pekao now surpassing Dino Polska as the most held. Dino Polska is analyzed in detail: a 100 billion SEK market cap grocery chain with ~3,000 standardized 400 sqm stores in smaller Polish cities and rural areas. The company has strong competitive advantages through vertical integration (own meat processing, construction company, properties), resulting in high margins (27% gross, 9% EBITDA) and 20%+ ROIC. However, the stock is down 25% from peak due to concerns about declining like-for-like growth and increasing competition. Other discussed stocks include Bank Pekao, Warsaw Stock Exchange, CD Projekt Red, and iFirma. The hosts also cover recent market events including Fed rate expectations and various company news.
key_takeaways: Polen har visat stark BNP-tillväxt på 4% per år sedan 1990 och förväntas växa 3% fram till 2030
Polska börsen har stigit 40% sedan årsskiftet
Dino Polska har unik affärsmodell med standardiserade butiker, vertikal integration och ägande av fastigheter
Dino Polska handlas till P/E 24 mot historiskt P/E 35 efter 25% kursfall
Bank Pekao har hög ROE på 19% men värderingen har stigit till P/B 1,8x mot historiskt 1,3x
Polen har hög sparande på sparkonton (över 50%) vilket kan driva börsintresset framöver
